key_insight: Distal weight-bearing implant performance depends on jointly designing load-bearing geometry, biomaterial surfaces, and bone–implant interfaces rather than optimizing coatings alone.
engineering_relevance: Gait-aware mechanical design and durable metallic, ceramic, or graded Ti–hydroxyapatite interfaces are essential to managing cyclic loads, micromotion, and long-term fixation.
method: Systematic review of implant concepts, geometry optimization, and gait-phase finite element analysis.
Synthesis of graded materials, interface durability, osseointegration, and clinical translation evidence.
Quantitative trend analysis of 34 direct-contribution papers and 32 empirical studies.
evidence_signal: More than half of the empirical evidence remained at bench or simulation level, with animal and human/clinical studies providing a smaller validation layer.
watch_item: Graded Ti–hydroxyapatite architectures are supported predominantly by non-DWBI analog studies, so DWBI-specific fatigue, coating-integrity, and biological validation remain necessary.
paper_title: Biomaterials and biomechanical design of distal weight-bearing implants: Computational modeling, biomaterial interfaces, and clinical translation
